[Discussion] Do you know any games that are worse than the sum of their parts?

GTA V online is the first game that comes to mind. The sheer amount of stuff in it is astonishing. I absolutely love the attention to detail. I really believe the devs care a great deal about this game, and it shows in all of the little things that are very easy to take for granted because it produces such a seamless and immersive experience.

Unfortunately the game tends to lose out when left in the middle of the city with no real goals, often turning in to deathmatch instead of capitalizing on everything else. I strongly believe the multiplayer is the biggest missed opportunity in the game.
Was writing a longer post about the Online specifically given I just came from a lobby chatting with someone about exactly this, but I'd actually say GTA V as a whole was pretty lackluster.

I thought the single player mode was actually quite good, especially for the person who likes to explore. To me, it was worth the price of admission. I think the problem is when you strip away the story and just leave the rest, it just isn't as entertaining - especially if like me you went in to it after 60 hours in single player.

Oh yeah, I totally get you on the price of admission point. I have to admit, it's not like I didn't have fun with it. I never actually got around to GTA IV when that was around (halfway through it now though), and I'm liking it much more than V. I think most of my thoughts lie with the 3-main-characters dynamic, which looked good on paper but got a poor execution (at least imo). I think it would've been better as 3 parts, with little nods to each other throughout (like Telltale's The Walking Dead 400 Days if you've played), and then a much bigger interlock at the end, where you can swap characters etc.

It was fun, but I didn't dick around with side missions etc as much as, say, San Andreas. The Online is fun with friends, but there's far too much grinding. I was actually chatting casually with hackers earlier about the state of the Online. Ironic indeed.

For me the worst offender of this will always be Jak 2. It was a blatant design by committee, driven by the current top 10 list of the time. I shameless aped Tony Hawk, Grand Theft Auto, Ratchet & Clank and more. The end result was a horrible game with a bunch of incongruous poorly fleshed out mechanics.

Man I hate that game.

Same. Personally I disliked it simply because of the GTA part of it - not my sort of thing - and I loved the platforming in the first one. I just figured it would be the same but in an urban setting and a darker story. I never finished it but I remember being really happy when I got to the mission where you had to go up the elevator and platform across a security bridge (or something) to get in the Baron's mansion. Great level and then it was back to GTA.

I didn't mind the skating hover board section. Could have been a fun mini-game/side-mission.

If you mean in terms of comparing a game series, I'd like to throw in the Mass Effect series.

In my opinion, ME1 was the best - it had proper RPG elements, wasn't made to be an all out shooter (yet still had plenty of the shooty-shooty, bang bang sections), and the choices mattered the most in terms of the plot, with a properly finished ending leaving you wanting more. The side quests were there if you wanted them (and the original loyalty missions which is how they should've been in ME2 :P), but wasn't like Skyrim or Fallout. You could easily blitz the main plot and still thoroughly enjoy the game.

ME2 was fun - really fun. The interrupting conversations was cool. The storming around as a renegade. Some of the side missions were quite fun, especially Kasumi's loyalty mission. Although I can't help but think the RPG-ness that made the first was watered down because there was a bigger audience given a PS3 release (with PS3'ers all like "hey, I've heard this is really, really good"), and so therefore became much more action-oriented. That and the Loyalty missions didn't really make any sense in relation to the ending, although it offered some nice exploration of the characters on your ship, but their recruitment offered enough background to know they could point a gun and shoot the baddies. Also, ME2 didn't actually advance the overall story arch of the Reaper invasion any further - the only real relation it had was humanity being targeted, which Shepard happened to be a part of.

ME3 continued the action-packed nature of ME2 given it's popularity, with most, if not all, RPG-ness gone by this point. I never actually completely finished it, despite buying all the DLC for it on sale, but it's not like we don't know how the ending for that turned out. Rather than the whole 'your choices don't matter', I like to think of it as a bit of 'too many doors left open' to have everyone live happily ever after - I personally think it should've gone downhill with no signs of stopping, and a last stand on Earth fighting an uphill struggle. It did have the co-op online, though, which whilst an absolute pain to get up and running, I remember thoroughly enjoying with some friends now and then.
